title: Scientific Achievements of the Han Dynasty
synopsis: The 400-year rule of the Han Dynasty generated many important inventions.

fullText.simplified:
汉朝学术成就

    汉朝持续了四百多年，有没有什么发明呢？
    当然有了。不仅有，而且很多还是造福人民、具有划时代意义的发明。下面我们就一起来看看吧！
    一、造纸术。
    如果你喜欢看中国的电视，就会发现汉朝以前的中国人是在竹子上、布上写字的。直到汉朝早期，才有人用麻做出了“麻纸”。这种纸非常轻，不像竹子那么重，也不像布那么贵。但这种麻纸有一些弊端，那就是，它是用植物直接做的，所以像干草一样粗糙，有很多植物纤维，画画、写字都很难。
    有一个叫蔡伦的人，发现了这个问题。他想了很多办法，想解决这个问题。比如他把纤维弄得细小一些，再做成麻纸，但试过以后发现用处不大。他又试着加入石灰，这样一来，粗糙的纤维就溶解了，水也变白了，但还剩下一些渣，还是不太好。
    他思索了很久，最后把材料都弄得很碎，又加了很多水。他只用网把表面的一层捞起来，晒干过后，就变成了一张又白又光滑的纸了！
    蔡伦的纸改变了大家的生活。皇帝对此赞叹不已，还把蔡伦封为了“侯爵”。后来的人都叫这种纸为“蔡侯纸”。
    二、地震仪。
    如果没有科技，人就很容易相信神。在很久以前，如果中国地震了，大家都会觉得是神仙生气了，皇帝就得出来道歉，说说自己哪里做得不好。而且，中国非常大。距离远，沟通就很困难。如果一个地方地震了，皇帝可能要一两个星期才知道。
    有一个叫张衡的人，发明了“地震仪”。从那以后，地震对于皇帝来说不再是神的惩罚，而是可以观测的、可以立刻知道的事情。
    张衡用金属制作了一个圆桶，看上去像个大酒桶。这个圆桶周围可不一般。它的周围有八条龙，嘴里都咬着一颗小球，地上对应着八只张着嘴巴的蛤蟆。
    八条龙头分别朝着东、西、南、北等八个不同的方向。不论哪里发生了地震，那个方向的龙立刻就会张开嘴，吐出小球。小球一下子掉到蛤蟆嘴里，声音非常清脆，人们马上就可以知道，龙头对着的那个方向地震了。
    刚开始人们还不相信，心想：“地震是神的惩罚，我们怎么可以观测呢？”直到有一天，朝西边的那条龙突然张开嘴巴，吐出了小球。皇帝问了大家，得知城里的人都没感觉到地震，但张衡坚持说：“那个方向一定有地震。”有人起哄说张衡吹牛，觉得张衡做的这个小玩意儿中看不中用。想不到，几天后西边真的传来了地震的消息，验证了“地震仪”的准确性。大家都对张衡的智慧钦佩极了。
    三、中医。
    你如果在中国的医院看病，很可能会发现一个国外没有的科室——中医科。中医可以选择按摩、针灸、药浴，用这些办法来缓解病人的疼痛。
    早在汉朝，就有一位杰出的中医叫张仲景，人们把他称作“医圣”。他知道中国的病人很多，医生很少，而且医生的水平参差不齐。所以，他决心写一本书，让所有医生都有看病的标准。
    他到处奔波，收集了许多有效的药方，写出了《伤寒杂病论》。这本著作是中国医学史上影响最大的古典医著之一，也是中国第一部临床治疗学方面的巨著。
    汉朝还有一位神医叫华佗。他也是中医中的泰斗，他的医术和张仲景不相上下。
    以前很多病需要开刀，但是病人不能忍受这种剧痛。后来，华佗发明了麻醉术，亲自抢救了很多需要做手术的病人。
    为了让人们防治疾病，锻炼身体，华佗还观察了老虎、鹿、熊、猿和鸟五种动物，把它们的动作画下来，编写成了《五禽戏》，鼓励人们学着做。这些锻炼的动作至今都还有人会，这就是中国最早的健身操。
fullText.traditional:
漢朝學術成就

    漢朝持續了四百多年，有沒有什麼發明呢？
    當然有了。不僅有，而且很多還是造福人民、具有劃時代意義的發明。下面我們就一起來看看吧！
    一、造紙術。
    如果你喜歡看中國的電視，就會發現漢朝以前的中國人是在竹子上、布上寫字的。直到漢朝早期，才有人用麻做出了“麻紙”。這種紙非常輕，不像竹子那麼重，也不像布那麼貴。但這種麻紙有一些弊端，那就是，它是用植物直接做的，所以像乾草一樣粗糙，有很多植物纖維，畫畫、寫字都很難。
    有一個叫蔡倫的人，發現了這個問題。他想了很多辦法，想解決這個問題。比如他把纖維弄得細小一些，再做成麻紙，但試過以後發現用處不大。他又試著加入石灰，這樣一來，粗糙的纖維就溶解了，水也變白了，但還剩下一些渣，還是不太好。
    他思索了很久，最後把材料都弄得很碎，又加了很多水。他只用網把表面的一層撈起來，曬乾過後，就變成了一張又白又光滑的紙了！
    蔡倫的紙改變了大家的生活。皇帝對此贊嘆不已，還把蔡倫封為了“侯爵”。後來的人都叫這種紙為“蔡侯紙”。
    二、地震儀。
    如果沒有科技，人就很容易相信神。在很久以前，如果中國地震了，大家都會覺得是神仙生氣了，皇帝就得出來道歉，說說自己哪裡做得不好。而且，中國非常大。距離遠，溝通就很困難。如果一個地方地震了，皇帝可能要一兩個星期才知道。
    有一個叫張衡的人，發明了“地震儀”。從那以後，地震對於皇帝來說不再是神的懲罰，而是可以觀測的、可以立刻知道的事情。
    張衡用金屬製作了一個圓桶，看上去像個大酒桶。這個圓桶周圍可不一般。它的周圍有八條龍，嘴裡都咬著一顆小球，地上對應著八隻張著嘴巴的蛤蟆。
    八條龍頭分別朝著東、西、南、北等八個不同的方向。不論哪裡發生了地震，那個方向的龍立刻就會張開嘴，吐出小球。小球一下子掉到蛤蟆嘴裡，聲音非常清脆，人們馬上就可以知道，龍頭對著的那個方向地震了。
    剛開始人們還不相信，心想：“地震是神的懲罰，我們怎麼可以觀測呢？”直到有一天，朝西邊的那條龍突然張開嘴巴，吐出了小球。皇帝問了大家，得知城裡的人都沒感覺到地震，但張衡堅持說：“那個方向一定有地震。”有人起鬨說張衡吹牛，覺得張衡做的這個小玩意兒中看不中用。想不到，幾天後西邊真的傳來了地震的消息，驗證了“地震儀”的準確性。大家都對張衡的智慧欽佩極了。
    三、中醫。
    你如果在中國的醫院看病，很可能會發現一個國外沒有的科室——中醫科。中醫可以選擇按摩、針灸、藥浴，用這些辦法來緩解病人的疼痛。
    早在漢朝，就有一位傑出的中醫叫張仲景，人們把他稱作“醫聖”。他知道中國的病人很多，醫生很少，而且醫生的水平參差不齊。所以，他決心寫一本書，讓所有醫生都有看病的標準。
    他到處奔波，收集了許多有效的藥方，寫出了《傷寒雜病論》。這本著作是中國醫學史上影響最大的古典醫著之一，也是中國第一部臨床治療學方面的巨著。
    漢朝還有一位神醫叫華佗。他也是中醫中的泰斗，他的醫術和張仲景不相上下。
    以前很多病需要開刀，但是病人不能忍受這種劇痛。後來，華佗發明了麻醉術，親自搶救了很多需要做手術的病人。
    為了讓人們防治疾病，鍛鍊身體，華佗還觀察了老虎、鹿、熊、猿和鳥五種動物，把牠們的動作畫下來，編寫成了《五禽戲》，鼓勵人們學著做。這些鍛鍊的動作至今都還有人會，這就是中國最早的健身操。

sentences.simplified: 而是可以观测的、可以立刻知道的事情。
sentences.traditional: 而是可以觀測的、可以立刻知道的事情。
sentences.pinyin: ér shì kě yǐ guān cè de kě yǐ lì kè zhī dào de shì qing
sentences.english: From then on, earthquakes were no longer a divine punishment for the emperor.
Rather, they could be observed and known about immediately.

sentences.simplified: 张衡用金属制作了一个圆桶，看上去像个大酒桶。
sentences.traditional: 張衡用金屬製作了一個圓桶，看上去像個大酒桶。
sentences.pinyin: zhāng héng yòng jīn shǔ zhì zuò le yí ge yuán tǒng kàn shàng qù xiàng ge dà jiǔ tǒng

sentences.simplified: 这个圆桶周围可不一般。
sentences.traditional: 這個圓桶周圍可不一般。
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge yuán tǒng zhōu wéi kě bú yì bān
sentences.english: Zhang Heng made a round barrel out of metal that looked like a large wine barrel.

sentences.simplified: 它的周围有八条龙，嘴里都咬着一颗小球，
sentences.traditional: 它的周圍有八條龍，嘴裡都咬著一顆小球，
sentences.pinyin: tā de zhōu wéi yǒu bā tiáo lóng zuǐ lǐ dōu yǎo zhe yì kē xiǎo qiú
sentences.english: The space surrounding the round barrel was anything but ordinary.

sentences.simplified: 地上对应着八只张着嘴巴的蛤蟆。
sentences.traditional: 地上對應著八隻張著嘴巴的蛤蟆。
sentences.pinyin: dì shang duì yìng zhe bā zhī zhāng zhe zuǐ ba de há ma
sentences.english: Surrounding the barrel were eight dragons, each holding a small ball in its mouth.
On the ground, there were eight corresponding toads with their mouths open.

sentences.simplified: 八条龙头分别朝着东、西、南、北等八个不同的方向。
sentences.traditional: 八條龍頭分別朝著東、西、南、北等八個不同的方向。
sentences.pinyin: bā tiáo lóng tóu fēn bié cháo zhe dōng xī nán běi děng bā ge bù tóng de fāng xiàng

sentences.simplified: 不论哪里发生了地震，那个方向的龙立刻就会张开嘴，吐出小球。
sentences.traditional: 不論哪裡發生了地震，那個方向的龍立刻就會張開嘴，吐出小球。
sentences.pinyin: bú lùn nǎ lǐ fā shēng le dì zhèn nà ge fāng xiàng de lóng lì kè jiù huì zhāng kāi zuǐ tǔ chū xiǎo qiú
sentences.english: The eight dragons were facing eight different directions, east, west, south, north, and so on.

sentences.simplified: 小球一下子掉到蛤蟆嘴里，声音非常清脆，
sentences.traditional: 小球一下子掉到蛤蟆嘴裡，聲音非常清脆，
sentences.pinyin: xiǎo qiú yí xià zi diào dào há ma zuǐ lǐ shēng yīn fēi cháng qīng cuì
sentences.english: Regardless of where an earthquake happened, the dragon facing that direction would immediately open its mouth and spat out the small ball.

sentences.simplified: 人们马上就可以知道，龙头对着的那个方向地震了。
sentences.traditional: 人們馬上就可以知道，龍頭對著的那個方向地震了。
sentences.pinyin: rén men mǎ shàng jiù kě yǐ zhī dào lóng tóu duì zhe de nà ge fāng xiàng dì zhèn le
sentences.english: The small ball would drop into the toad’s mouth with a very clear and sharp sound.
People would then immediately know that there was an earthquake in the direction that the dragon’s head was facing.

sentences.simplified: 刚开始人们还不相信，心想：“地震是神的惩罚，我们怎么可以观测呢？”
sentences.traditional: 剛開始人們還不相信，心想：“地震是神的懲罰，我們怎麼可以觀測呢？”
sentences.pinyin: gāng kāi shǐ rén men hái bù xiāng xìn xīn xiǎng dì zhèn shì shén de chéng fá wǒ men zěn me kě yǐ guān cè ne

sentences.simplified: 直到有一天，朝西边的那条龙突然张开嘴巴，吐出了小球。
sentences.traditional: 直到有一天，朝西邊的那條龍突然張開嘴巴，吐出了小球。
sentences.pinyin: zhí dào yǒu yì tiān cháo xī biān de nà tiáo lóng tū rán zhāng kāi zuǐ ba tǔ chū le xiǎo qiú
sentences.english: At first, people didn’t believe this. They thought, “Earthquakes are a punishment from the gods. How could we observe them?”

sentences.simplified: 皇帝问了大家，得知城里的人都没感觉到地震，
sentences.traditional: 皇帝問了大家，得知城裡的人都沒感覺到地震，
sentences.pinyin: huáng dì wèn le dà jiā dé zhī chéng lǐ de rén dōu méi gǎn jué dào dì zhèn
sentences.english: One day, the dragon facing west opened its mouth and spit out the small ball.

sentences.simplified: 但张衡坚持说：“那个方向一定有地震。”
sentences.traditional: 但張衡堅持說：“那個方向一定有地震。”
sentences.pinyin: dàn zhāng héng jiān chí shuō nà ge fāng xiàng yí dìng yǒu dì zhèn
sentences.english: The emperor asked around and learned that no one in the city felt an earthquake.

sentences.simplified: 有人起哄说张衡吹牛，觉得张衡做的这个小玩意儿中看不中用。
sentences.traditional: 有人起鬨說張衡吹牛，覺得張衡做的這個小玩意兒中看不中用。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu rén qǐ hòng shuō zhāng héng chuī niú jué de zhāng héng zuò de zhè ge xiǎo wán yì'r zhōng kàn bù zhōng yòng
sentences.english: But Zhang Heng insisted and said, “There must have been an earthquake in that direction.”

sentences.simplified: 想不到，几天后西边真的传来了地震的消息，验证了“地震仪”的准确性。
sentences.traditional: 想不到，幾天後西邊真的傳來了地震的消息，驗證了“地震儀”的準確性。
sentences.pinyin: xiǎng bú dào jǐ tiān hòu xī biān zhēn de chuán lái le dì zhèn de xiāo xi yàn zhèng le dì zhèn yí de zhǔn què xìng
sentences.english: People heckled, saying that Zhang Heng was bluffing. They thought that this little gadget Zhang Heng created was useless.

sentences.simplified: 大家都对张衡的智慧钦佩极了。
sentences.traditional: 大家都對張衡的智慧欽佩極了。
sentences.pinyin: dà jiā dōu duì zhāng héng de zhì huì qīn pèi jí le
sentences.english: Unexpectedly, a few days later, news of an earthquake really did come from the west, verifying the accuracy of the “seismograph”.
Everyone greatly admired Zhang Heng’s wisdom.

sentences.simplified: 三、中医。
sentences.traditional: 三、中醫。
sentences.pinyin: sān zhōng yī

sentences.english: 3. Traditional Chinese Medicine

sentences.simplified: 你如果在中国的医院看病，很可能会发现一个国外没有的科室——中医科。
sentences.traditional: 你如果在中國的醫院看病，很可能會發現一個國外沒有的科室——中醫科。
sentences.pinyin: nǐ rú guǒ zài zhōng guó de yī yuàn kàn bìng hěn kě néng huì fā xiàn yí ge guó wài méi yǒu de kē shì zhōng yī kē

sentences.simplified: 中医可以选择按摩、针灸、药浴，用这些办法来缓解病人的疼痛。
sentences.traditional: 中醫可以選擇按摩、針灸、藥浴，用這些辦法來緩解病人的疼痛。
sentences.pinyin: zhōng yī kě yǐ xuǎn zé àn mó zhēn jiǔ yào yù yòng zhè xiē bàn fǎ lái huǎn jiě bìng rén de téng tòng
sentences.english: If you visit a hospital in China, you may find a department that does not exist abroad—the department of traditional Chinese medicine.
Doctors of traditional Chinese medicine can use methods such as massages, acupuncture, and medicinal baths to relieve a patient’s pain.

sentences.simplified: 早在汉朝，就有一位杰出的中医叫张仲景，
sentences.traditional: 早在漢朝，就有一位傑出的中醫叫張仲景，
sentences.pinyin: zǎo zài hàn cháo jiù yǒu yí wèi jié chū de zhōng yī jiào zhāng zhòng jǐng

sentences.simplified: 人们把他称作“医圣”。
sentences.traditional: 人們把他稱作“醫聖”。
sentences.pinyin: rén men bǎ tā chēng zuò yī shèng
sentences.english: As early as the Han dynasty, there was an outstanding doctor of traditional Chinese medicine named Zhang Zhongjing.

sentences.simplified: 他知道中国的病人很多，医生很少，而且医生的水平参差不齐。
sentences.traditional: 他知道中國的病人很多，醫生很少，而且醫生的水平參差不齊。
sentences.pinyin: tā zhī dào zhōng guó de bìng rén hěn duō yī shēng hěn shǎo ér qiě yī shēng de shuǐ píng cēn cī bù qí
sentences.english: People called him the “Medical Sage”.

sentences.simplified: 所以，他决心写一本书，让所有医生都有看病的标准。
sentences.traditional: 所以，他決心寫一本書，讓所有醫生都有看病的標準。
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ tā jué xīn xiě yì běn shū ràng suǒ yǒu yī shēng dōu yǒu kàn bìng de biāo zhǔn
sentences.english: He knew that there were many patients and few doctors in China, and moreover, the doctors were of varying proficiency.
So, he resolved to write a book to teach all doctors the standards for treating patients.

sentences.simplified: 他到处奔波，收集了许多有效的药方，写出了《伤寒杂病论》。
sentences.traditional: 他到處奔波，收集了許多有效的藥方，寫出了《傷寒雜病論》。
sentences.pinyin: tā dào chù bēn bō shōu jí le xǔ duō yǒu xiào de yào fāng xiě chū le shāng hán zá bìng lún

sentences.simplified: 这本著作是中国医学史上影响最大的古典医著之一，
sentences.traditional: 這本著作是中國醫學史上影響最大的古典醫著之一，
sentences.pinyin: zhè běn zhù zuò shì zhōng guó yī xué shǐ shang yǐng xiǎng zuì dà de gǔ diǎn yī zhù zhī yī
sentences.english: He was constantly traveling. He collected many effective remedies and wrote the “Treatise on Cold Pathogenic and Miscellaneous Diseases”.

sentences.simplified: 也是中国第一部临床治疗学方面的巨著。
sentences.traditional: 也是中國第一部臨床治療學方面的巨著。
sentences.pinyin: yě shì zhōng guó dì yī bù lín chuáng zhì liáo xué fāng miàn de jù zhù
sentences.english: This work is one of the most influential classical medical books in the history of traditional Chinese medicine.
It is also the first monumental Chinese work on clinical treatment.

sentences.simplified: 汉朝还有一位神医叫华佗。
sentences.traditional: 漢朝還有一位神醫叫華佗。
sentences.pinyin: hàn cháo hái yǒu yí wèi shén yī jiào huà tuó

sentences.simplified: 他也是中医中的泰斗，他的医术和张仲景不相上下。
sentences.traditional: 他也是中醫中的泰斗，他的醫術和張仲景不相上下。
sentences.pinyin: tā yě shì zhōng yī zhōng de tài dǒu tā de yī shù hé zhāng zhòng jǐng bù xiāng shàng xià
sentences.english: The Han dynasty had another miracle-working doctor named Hua Tuo.
He was also a leading scholar of traditional Chinese medicine, and his medical skill matched that of Zhang Zhongjing.

sentences.simplified: 以前很多病需要开刀，但是病人不能忍受这种剧痛。
sentences.traditional: 以前很多病需要開刀，但是病人不能忍受這種劇痛。
sentences.pinyin: yǐ qián hěn duō bìng xū yào kāi dāo dàn shì bìng rén bù néng rěn shòu zhè zhǒng jù tòng

sentences.simplified: 后来，华佗发明了麻醉术，亲自抢救了很多需要做手术的病人。
sentences.traditional: 後來，華佗發明了麻醉術，親自搶救了很多需要做手術的病人。
sentences.pinyin: hòu lái huà tuó fā míng le má zuì shù qīn zì qiǎng jiù le hěn duō xū yào zuò shǒu shù de bìng rén
sentences.english: In the past, many illnesses required surgery, but patients were not able to withstand the severe pain.
Later, Hua Tuo invented anesthesia and personally saved many patients who needed surgery.

sentences.simplified: 为了让人们防治疾病，锻炼身体，华佗还观察了老虎、鹿、熊、猿和鸟五种动物，
sentences.traditional: 為了讓人們防治疾病，鍛鍊身體，華佗還觀察了老虎、鹿、熊、猿和鳥五種動物，
sentences.pinyin: wèi le ràng rén men fáng zhì jí bìng duàn liàn shēn tǐ huà tuó hái guān chá le lǎo hǔ lù xióng yuán hé niǎo wǔ zhǒng dòng wù

sentences.simplified: 把它们的动作画下来，编写成了《五禽戏》，
sentences.traditional: 把牠們的動作畫下來，編寫成了《五禽戲》，
sentences.pinyin: bǎ tā men de dòng zuò huà xià lái biān xiě chéng le wǔ qín xì
sentences.english: In order to help people prevent disease and get exercise, Hua Tuo observed five animals: tiger, deer, bear, ape, and bird.

sentences.simplified: 鼓励人们学着做。
sentences.traditional: 鼓勵人們學著做。
sentences.pinyin: gǔ lì rén men xué zhe zuò
sentences.english: He drew the movements of these five animals and compiled them into the “Five Animal Qigong Exercises”.

sentences.simplified: 这些锻炼的动作至今都还有人会，这就是中国最早的健身操。
sentences.traditional: 這些鍛鍊的動作至今都還有人會，這就是中國最早的健身操。
sentences.pinyin: zhè xiē duàn liàn de dòng zuò zhì jīn dōu hái yǒu rén huì zhè jiù shì zhōng guó zuì zǎo de jiàn shēn cāo
sentences.english: He encouraged people to learn the exercises and follow along.

sentence_translations: Scientific Achievements of the Han Dynasty
The Han Dynasty lasted for more than 400 years. Were there any inventions?
Of course, there were. Not only that, many of these inventions benefited the people and had epoch-making significance.
Let’s take a look!
1. Papermaking
If you like watching Chinese TV, you will discover that before the Han Dynasty, Chinese people would write on bamboo or cloth.
It was only during the early Han Dynasty that people used hemp to make “hemp paper”.
This paper was very light. It was not heavy like bamboo and not expensive like cloth.
But this type of hemp paper had a disadvantage, which was that it was made directly from plants.
This made it rough like hay with many plant fibers. It was very difficult to draw and write on.
There was a man named Cai Lun who discovered this problem.
He thought up a lot of ideas, wanting to solve this problem.
For example, he made the fibers finer before making them into hemp paper, but after trying it, he found that this wasn’t very useful.
He then tried adding lime. The rough fibers dissolved, and the water turned white, but there was still some deposit left.
This solution was still not very good.
He thought about this for a long time.
In the end, he broke all of the materials into very small pieces and added a lot of water.
He then used a net to scoop up only the surface layer. After drying, it turned into a sheet of white, smooth paper!
Cai Lun’s paper changed everyone’s lives.
The emperor was full of praise, and he also granted Cai Lun the title of “marquis”.
Later, people would call this type of paper “paper of Marquis Cai”.
2. Seismograph
Without science and technology, it is very easy for people to believe in gods.
A long time ago, if there was an earthquake in China, everyone would believe that the gods were angry.
The emperor would then come to apologize and say what he did wrong.
China is also very big, and the distance made communication difficult.
If there was an earthquake somewhere, it might have been one or two weeks until the emperor found out about it.
There was a man named Zhang Heng who invented the “seismograph”.
From then on, earthquakes were no longer a divine punishment for the emperor.
Rather, they could be observed and known about immediately.
Zhang Heng made a round barrel out of metal that looked like a large wine barrel.
The space surrounding the round barrel was anything but ordinary.
Surrounding the barrel were eight dragons, each holding a small ball in its mouth.
On the ground, there were eight corresponding toads with their mouths open.
The eight dragons were facing eight different directions, east, west, south, north, and so on.
Regardless of where an earthquake happened, the dragon facing that direction would immediately open its mouth and spat out the small ball.
The small ball would drop into the toad’s mouth with a very clear and sharp sound.
People would then immediately know that there was an earthquake in the direction that the dragon’s head was facing.
At first, people didn’t believe this. They thought, “Earthquakes are a punishment from the gods. How could we observe them?”
One day, the dragon facing west opened its mouth and spit out the small ball.
The emperor asked around and learned that no one in the city felt an earthquake.
But Zhang Heng insisted and said, “There must have been an earthquake in that direction.”
People heckled, saying that Zhang Heng was bluffing. They thought that this little gadget Zhang Heng created was useless.
Unexpectedly, a few days later, news of an earthquake really did come from the west, verifying the accuracy of the “seismograph”.
Everyone greatly admired Zhang Heng’s wisdom.
3. Traditional Chinese Medicine
If you visit a hospital in China, you may find a department that does not exist abroad—the department of traditional Chinese medicine.
Doctors of traditional Chinese medicine can use methods such as massages, acupuncture, and medicinal baths to relieve a patient’s pain.
As early as the Han dynasty, there was an outstanding doctor of traditional Chinese medicine named Zhang Zhongjing.
People called him the “Medical Sage”.
He knew that there were many patients and few doctors in China, and moreover, the doctors were of varying proficiency.
So, he resolved to write a book to teach all doctors the standards for treating patients.
He was constantly traveling. He collected many effective remedies and wrote the “Treatise on Cold Pathogenic and Miscellaneous Diseases”.
This work is one of the most influential classical medical books in the history of traditional Chinese medicine.
It is also the first monumental Chinese work on clinical treatment.
The Han dynasty had another miracle-working doctor named Hua Tuo.
He was also a leading scholar of traditional Chinese medicine, and his medical skill matched that of Zhang Zhongjing.
In the past, many illnesses required surgery, but patients were not able to withstand the severe pain.
Later, Hua Tuo invented anesthesia and personally saved many patients who needed surgery.
In order to help people prevent disease and get exercise, Hua Tuo observed five animals: tiger, deer, bear, ape, and bird.
He drew the movements of these five animals and compiled them into the “Five Animal Qigong Exercises”.
He encouraged people to learn the exercises and follow along.
These exercises are still known today, and this was the earliest form of aerobics in China.
